home.title: Spindro: free, open-source indoor cycling app for smart trainers
home.description: Free, open-source indoor cycling app. ERG and virtual gears for your smart trainer, structured workouts and six games that are workouts. No subscription, no account. Browser and Android.

faq.a: Yes. No subscription, no ads, no in-app purchases. The source code is open on GitHub. The project is run by one person; you can help with bug reports, trainer reports and code.
No. You open the app and ride. Your rides, records and settings stay on your device. You can export a backup to move them to another device.

faq.q: Does it work on iPhone and iPad?
faq.a: Not in Safari: Apple does not allow Web Bluetooth there. A browser that adds Web Bluetooth, such as Bluefy, should work; we have not tested it. A native iOS app may come later.

faq.q: Which browser and device do I need?
faq.a: Android: Chrome, or the Android app. PC, Mac, Linux and ChromeOS: Chrome or Edge with Bluetooth. The page must be served over HTTPS.

Spindro talks FTMS, the standard Bluetooth protocol most smart trainers of recent years use. We have ridden one trainer for real. The compatibility page says what is verified, what should work, and how to report yours.

It does the trainer side: ERG, virtual gears, structured workouts and games. It is not an online virtual world: there is no multiplayer. A trainer accepts one Bluetooth connection at a time, so close other apps first.

faq.q: Can I write my own game?
faq.a: Yes. The games share a kit and a set of design rules. Start from the Build a game page.

faq.q: What happens to my data and privacy?
faq.a: This website has no cookies and no ads, and its fonts are served from the same site. We count visits anonymously with GoatCounter, with no cookies and no personal data. In the app, ride data stays on your device, and anonymous usage counting only starts if you agree. Data leaves the device only if you use Strava (it sends the ride to Strava), play a YouTube video (Google's player loads) or export a file. Read the privacy policy for the details.

home.kicker: Indoor cycling app · free and open source
home.lead: Spindro connects to your smart trainer over Bluetooth. Start a ride in ERG, follow a structured workout, or play games that run on your real watts. It works in the browser and on Android, with no account.
home.heroNote: Android: Chrome or the app. PC and Mac: Chrome or Edge. iPhone: the Bluefy browser.
home.heroAlt: The Spindro home screen with a trainer connected: a free ride in ERG with a 130 W target and a Start button, and shortcuts to workouts, games and history.

stages.title: Add a device, then ride
stages.text: The home is built around ERG: a Today card with a target in watts, − and + to change it, and one big Start button. One “Add device” button pairs a trainer, a Zwift controller, a heart rate strap, a power meter or a cadence sensor, and the app works out what each one is for.
stages.alt: The Devices sheet listing a connected Van Rysel D100 trainer and a heart rate strap, each with a Disconnect button, and the Add another device button.
rows: FTMS first; Tacx FE-C and Wahoo legacy as fallbacks
Zwift Click, Play and Ride as shifters and remote
Shows which key the app receives and lets you map it

stages.title: Train with a plan
stages.text: Structured workouts and multi-week plans, scaled to your FTP. If you do not know it, a ramp test estimates it. While a workout runs, the cockpit shows the current step, the time left and the next one.
stages.alt: A workout in progress: 196 watts, a Sweet spot 3×10 workout in its warm-up with the step profile and the next step.

stages.title: Games that are workouts
stages.text: Six 3D games, each one a structured workout in percent of your FTP: 5, 10 or 20 minutes, three levels, efforts and recoveries, something to do every few seconds. They share one menu, so you learn it once.

stages.title: Your watch keeps the ride
stages.text: On Android the phone can broadcast power, cadence and speed as a Bluetooth sensor, so your watch records the ride and syncs it the way it always does. The app also keeps its own history.
stages.alt: Ride summary with time, distance, average power, kilojoules and power records.
rows: Built for Garmin; other watches should work
.fit with the GPS track of a loaded route

games: A timed stage: breakaway, intermediate sprint, climb and final sprint. Climbs load your trainer.
Hold the road against waves of zombies. More watts, more shots.
A runner shooter. Shields break only at the right watts; a sprint unleashes overdrive.
Bridge to the riders who attack and tow them into your slipstream.
A pedal-powered plane: your watts are your altitude. Fly the rings that draw your workout.
Bounce a bottle off the soigneurs. Cadence sets its speed, watts charge the turbo.
home.gamesMore: The games menu also plays any YouTube ride video, or a video of your own, at your own speed.
gamesAlt: Breakaway: the rider in pink leads a pack toward the sea, with the gear, the climb goal and a profile of the stage on screen.
Horde Run: a rider on a night road firing at a horde of zombies, with wave counter and shots per second.
Pedal Strike: a rider on a road lined with shipping containers, with score, timer, hearts, the workout step bar and the overdrive meter.
Slipstream: a rider on a country road collecting bottles, with the next rider 45 metres ahead.
Updraft: a yellow plane carrying the rider through a ring, with an altitude gauge.
Feed Zone: a rider bouncing a bottle off a line of fans holding buckets.
ownPoints: No subscription, no ads, no in-app purchases.
No account. Your rides stay on your device.
GPL-3.0: the code is public and stays public.
Five languages. Works offline once loaded.
Visits to this site are counted anonymously; the app asks before it counts anything.
home.compatLead: An honest table. One trainer has been ridden for real, and so have the + and − keys of one Zwift Click. The rest is built from public specifications and tested against simulated devices.
home.finalText: Open the web app, connect the trainer, ride. It takes about a minute.
home.gamesFollow: A game can also follow the workout you are riding.
home.devLead: Every Spindro game is a small JavaScript module on a shared kit: 3D scene, power and cadence, one menu, results, audio and progress. No bundler, no build step. If you can write a canvas or three.js game, you can add one.
devPoints: A game kit: menu, results, HUD, cyclist, environment, quality settings.
Power and cadence from the trainer, or a demo rider when none is connected.
Design rules that keep a game a workout: sessions in % of FTP, three levels.

compat.title: Compatible trainers and watches | Spindro
compat.description: Smart trainers, Zwift controllers and watches that work with Spindro, and how sure we are: ridden for real, should work, reported by users. Only one trainer has been tested on real hardware.
compat.lead: Spindro picks the protocol on its own: FTMS, then Tacx FE-C over Bluetooth, then Wahoo legacy, then read-only Cycling Power or Speed & Cadence. Below is what we support and how sure we are.

statusDesc.verified: Tested on the real device by the author.
statusDesc.expected: The protocol is supported by the code, but this model has never been tried.
statusDesc.reported: Users told us it works. No report has been collected yet.
statusDesc.partial: Some functions were tested on the real device; the rest was not.

compat.reportText: Tried a trainer or watch? In the app, use “Report a problem”, or open an issue on GitHub with the model, what worked and what did not. Reports turn “should work” into “reported by users”.
compat.note: Tacx FE-C and Wahoo legacy support have been tested only against a simulated trainer. A trainer that accepts only one Bluetooth connection cannot be used by Spindro and another app at the same time.

dev.title: Build a game for Spindro | Spindro
dev.description: How to add a game to Spindro: the game kit, the design rules, the steps to follow and where the code lives. Open source, plain JavaScript, no build step.
dev.lead: Spindro's games are small JavaScript modules on a shared kit. This page says what the kit gives you, what rules a game follows, and how to add one. It does not document an API: the code is the reference, and a written guide is on its way.
kit: Live watts and cadence from the trainer or sensors, smoothed for you. With no trainer connected, a demo rider keeps the game playable.
Length (5, 10 or 20 minutes), level (easy, normal, hard), start by key, touch or pedalling; stars and personal bests at the end.
Text, panels and messages that do not overlap and stay readable at arm's length.
A 3D cyclist, scenery helpers, audio, particle effects and an automatic quality setting.
+ and − from a Zwift Click or the keyboard reach your game as a single input(±1) call.
Experience points, records and achievements shared across games.
rules: A session is a workout: 5, 10 or 20 minutes, with intensity in percent of the player's FTP, so it is fair at 120 W and at 320 W.
Three levels (easy, normal, hard) and a difficulty that adapts a little after failed or successful efforts.
Something to do within eight seconds, and never more than five seconds without an event that asks or rewards something.
Playable without touching the screen: watts and cadence do the work, + and − do one thing, spelled out in the menu.
Whoever stops pedalling pauses the game; nobody is punished for pushing harder.
dev.stepsTitle: Adding a game, step by step
steps: Read the existing games in the js/games folder: each is one module plus a small plan file that describes its workout.
Copy the closest one, and give your game its own id and its own i18n keys in all five locales.
Describe the workout as a plan in percent of FTP, and let the kit's menu and results screen handle the rest.
Register the game in js/app.js so it appears in the games list, and add its files to the ASSETS list in sw.js.
Test it with the simulated trainer in tests/fake-ble.js, at several power levels, then run the whole test suite.
Send a pull request on GitHub.
dev.docsSoon: The written guide and API reference are still being written and are not in the repository yet. Until then, the games folder is the reference.
dev.folder: Browse the games folder on GitHub
dev.legal: Assets must have a clear licence (CC0, MIT, OFL, or generated for the project) and be credited. User-facing text goes through the translation files. The project is GPL-3.0.
